questions.q: According to this lesson's framework, what is the single most useful question to ask about an ML infrastructure component?
options: Which option is cheapest this quarter
Whether the component differentiates you, or is commodity infrastructure every ML team needs
Whether open source exists for it at all
Whether the CTO has a personal preference
questions.explain: The deciding factor is differentiation: whether building the component well actually improves your models and business, or whether it's commodity plumbing every team needs in roughly the same shape.

questions.q: Which of these is a 'point solution' rather than a fully managed end-to-end platform?
options: SageMaker
Vertex AI
Databricks Machine Learning
Tecton
questions.explain: Tecton is a best-of-breed feature store vendor — a point solution. SageMaker, Vertex AI, and Databricks ML are fully managed platforms that bundle multiple components together.

questions.q: What hidden cost does the lesson associate with self-hosting an open-source tool like Feast or MLflow?
options: A mandatory annual license fee
The team must own ongoing maintenance — upgrades, on-call, and retained institutional knowledge
Open-source tools cannot be customized at all
It automatically locks you into a single cloud vendor
questions.explain: Self-hosting avoids license fees but shifts the burden of upgrades, operational on-call, and institutional knowledge onto your own team — a cost that's easy to underestimate at adoption time.

questions.q: A startup has one small ML team and no component that's clearly unique to their business. What does the lesson recommend?
options: Build every component from scratch to avoid future lock-in
Start on a managed platform or open-source default, and only customize once a specific gap is clear
Hire a dedicated platform team before training any models
Wait until the company has hundreds of models before choosing any tooling
questions.explain: The practical heuristic is to start with a managed platform or an open-source default, since the team doesn't yet know its real requirements well enough to justify custom work.

questions.q: What risk does the lesson specifically call out about adopting a fully managed platform?
options: Managed platforms have no effect on long-term flexibility
Migrating away later can be expensive once years of pipelines are built against that vendor's APIs and pricing model
Managed platforms cannot bundle feature storage and training together
Managed platforms never offer a registry or serving tooling
questions.explain: Vendor lock-in is a real cost on the 'buy' side: once pipelines, APIs, and pricing assumptions are built around a managed platform, leaving it can take months of migration work.
